author: Cunningham
note: Preface to Garrick's tour: Barmayan monastery = Sri Gupta's monastery for Chinese pilgrims (Yijing, not Xiyu ji); Pushkalavati = Charsada named without Xuanzang

author: Garrick
asr_identification: Charsada (Bala Hissar mound), Peshawar district
evidence: Bala Hissar mound measured (irregular triangle, c. 485,000 sq ft at top); gates located (three, one 200 ft from W corner of N face) to follow the pilgrim's bearings
quote: the identification of Chdérsada with the ancient Peuke…nothing clearer or more satisfying can be imagined, as further research only goes to . confirm it
note: Garrick's report in vol. XIX (Cunningham's assistant). Agrees with Mizutani (Charsadda) and Cunningham 1871 (Hashtnagar/Charsada)

author: Garrick
asr_identification: stupa E of the city among the mounds of Shahr-i-Napursan, c. 3.5 miles E by N of the Bala Hissar; monastery and stupa N of the city = the 'Gumbaz' high mound near Utmanzai, Charsadda, Peshawar district
evidence: mounds at Shahr-i-Napursan; Garrick's own trial excavations and abandoned Sappers' trenches; high-peaked mound 'Gumbaz' with surrounding ruins
quote: Regarding the ‘“ stipa to east of city” mentioned by the Chinese pilgrim…there are several mounds within and without theremains of the city called Shhar-2-Wdparsan…I found a high-peaked mound which goes at present by the name of “the Gdambaz,” or cupola
note: new: stupa E of Puṣkalāvatī and monastery/stupa N of the city (not in the table). OCR '33 miles' = 3½ miles

author: Garrick
name_in_asr: Hwen Thsang's stipa to the east of Peukelaotis
asr_identification: excavated mound (Plate XXII) near Charsadda, Peshawar district, as probable site of the stupa E of Puṣkalāvatī
evidence: excavation of the mound: natural cavity 9 ft below surface, glazed pottery, 12-angled pierced copper bead
quote: a thorough exploration of this mound would doubtless bring to light many objects of interest, and probably Hwen Thsang’s stipa to the east of Peukelaotis
note: new: stupa E of Puṣkalāvatī (02.04.09 area). Tentative. Rest of passage (Jumalgarhi finds) not tied to Xuanzang

author: Cunningham
note: Mathura's religious history; Xuanzang's count of temples and monasteries, no location

author: Cunningham
note: Political history of Mathura (Sudra king in 635)

author: Cunningham
asr_identification: ancient (Aryan) city on the site of the Katra (Kesopura mahalla), with the Bhuteswar temple as centre, Mathura district; the Jumna then flowed in the Katra channel
evidence: ground examined with large-scale map; old river channel traced under the walls of the Katra; local unanimous tradition; Growse's conclusions
quote: 1 had already arrived at his secorid conclusion as to the site of the ancient Aryan city from an examination of the ground, compared with Hwen Thsang’s statements as to the relative positions of the different Biddhist monuments
note: Refines Ancient Geography (city since moved N and W): 7th-c. city placed by the old Katra channel. Mizutani gives the Mathurā district/town only

author: Cunningham
asr_identification: the present old fort on the bank of the Jumna, c. 1 mile E of the Katra, Mathura; 7th-c. city on the E (left) bank of the Katra channel
evidence: Tavernier on the river's change of course; Xuanzang's 5-6 li E with no river crossing; Fa-hian's crossing of the Jumna; Abu Rihan places Mathura on the E bank
quote: I take the monastery of Upagupta to be the present old fort on the bank of the Jumna, which’is just about 1 mile to the east of the Katra
note: Differs from Mizutani (Upagupta monastery cannot now be located). No identification of 04.07.03 in Ancient Geography (1871)

author: Cunningham
note: Abu Rihan/Rashid-ud-din on Mathura on the E bank of the Jumna in Mahmud's time; Xuanzang not used

author: Cunningham
note: Mahaban history; Sudra king of Mathura (no location)

author: Cunningham
note: Nalanda foundation legend quoted as a parallel to the Delhi iron pillar story

author: Cunningham
asr_identification: dragon cave = artificial cave (old quarry) in Pabhosa (Prabhasa) hill, 3 miles NW of Garhwa fort / 2 miles from Kosam and Pali; Vasubandhu's two-storeyed brick chamber = cave in the Tikri mound near Garauli and Gopsahsa, SE of the fort; Ghoshila monastery name preserved in Gopsahsa village; Allahabad district
evidence: Pabhosa cave with pillar, Jain temple, local Naga legend; Gupta-period rock inscriptions; Tikri mound 45-50 ft, two rooms measured (11 x 8 ft 3 in; 11 ft 6 in x 13 ft 3 in), brick wall of a lower storey; bricks and stone fragments round Gopsahsa; no stupa traces
quote: On reaching the hill of Pabhosa I found that there was not only a cave high up in the face of the hill, but that there was also a N^ga, or serpent…The brick wall I take to be the remains of a lower storey, which agrees with Hwen Thsang’s account of the residence of Vasubandhu…The name of Gos-irsha, or Gosira, appears to be preserved in that of the neighbouring village of Gopsahsa
note: new: dragon cave SW of Kauśāmbī; Vasubandhu's chamber. Pabhosa lies NW, not SW. Ghoṣila monastery placed at Gopsahsa SE of the fort, which differs from Mizutani (Sharma's Ghositārāma N of the E gate at Kosam). Revises his earlier search on the Jumna bank W of the city

author: Cunningham
asr_identification: Jejakabhukti (Jajahuti of Abu Rihan) = Bundelkhand, capital Khajuraha
evidence: inscriptions from Mahoba (Kirtti Varma) naming Jejakabhukti; Abu Rihan; distance from Ujain re-read as 84 kos (c. 250 miles)
quote: Khajuraha is described by Abu Rihan as the capital of the kingdom of J^ajdhuti — a name which recalls the Chi-clii-to of the Chinese pilgrim Hwen Thsang…I have found the name of the province in two different inscriptions
note: Confirms Ancient Geography (Jajhoti, capital Khajuraho) with epigraphic support; Mizutani undecided (Bundelkhand or Chitor)

author: Cunningham
asr_identification: Jejakabhukti/Jejahuti = Bundelkhand (Mahoba inscriptions)
evidence: inscription naming the country Jejakabhukti/Jejakasukti (Madanpur); Jajhaotiya Brahmans and Baniyas preserve the name
quote: Both of these forms would naturally be shortened to Jejd-hnii…That this was the actual name of the country we learn from two independent authorities of still older date. The first is the Chinese pilgrim Hwen Thsang, who visited Chichi-to
note: Epigraphic support for Cunningham 1871; Mizutani undecided

author: Cunningham
asr_identification: hill city not yet located; probably Ptolemy's Balanti-purgon (Chhattisgarh region)
quote: Their other town, named Balanti-furgouj is, most probably, the curious hill city described by the Chinese pilgrims Fa Hian and Hwen Thsang…The position of the city described by the Chinese writers from hearsay has not yet been ascertained
note: Withdraws to 'not yet ascertained' from Ancient Geography's rock monastery 50 miles W/SW of Chanda; places it with Ptolemy's Adisathri (Chhattisgarh), in line with the later Kosala revision; Mizutani: Pārāvata/Śrīparvata

author: Cunningham
asr_identification: lofty mound of Chini (Amritsar district)
evidence: mound dug by a brick contractor; very old Vishnu statue found
quote: I have described the lofty mound of Chini in my last Panjab Report, Volume XIV, page 53…I then identified it with the Chinapati of the pilgrim Hwen Thsang
note: Repeats ASR XIV, which revised Ancient Geography (Patti); close to Mizutani (Chiniyari)

author: Cunningham
name_in_asr: Ramagrama; Anoma; City of the Moriyas; Kusinagara
asr_identification: Ramagrama stupa = Ramnagar; Anoma = Kudawa Nala; three stupas of Chandaka's return, cut hair, changed garments = three mounds near the river; City of the Moriyas = Rajdhani, S of Gorakhpur; nirvana statue found at Kasia
evidence: Carlleyle's discovery of the colossal nirvana statue at Kasia in a brick-arched chamber, Gupta inscription on the pedestal
quote: Ramnagar, the site of the famous Stipa of Rémagrdma…The three Stiipas of ‘ Chandaka’s Return,” the “ Cut Hair,” and the “Changed Garments,” with three mounds i in the neighbourhood of the river…This statue must therefore be the identical one that was seen by the Chinese pilgrim
note: Cunningham's preface accepting Carlleyle's identifications: revises Ancient Geography (Ramagrama at Deokali, Anoma = Aumi, Chandaoli, Moriya ash stupa at Sahankat). Mizutani gives no Rāmagrāma site. Also endorses Carlleyle's 'discovery of Kapilavastu' (Bhuila Tal), later rejected

author: Carlleyle
asr_identification: Narayana temple = Narainpur, N bank of the Ganges opposite Masar (near Gangapur, Saran/Baliya); Asylum stupa = island at the Ghaghra mouth 5 miles E of Narainpur (washed away) or Godena near Revilganj; Drona stupa = Cheran (Chirand), Saran district (alt. Kandarbudha or Sarita Dih)
evidence: route of three old roads N from Masar to the ferry; old Narainpur villages and ruined temple (one washed away); Godena tradition of Gautama; Digwara examined, no mound; Cheran mound with mosque of Husain Shah built from a Hindu temple, ancient bricks and ring-wells
quote: It is this site at Narainpur that I would propose to identify with the Narayana or Na-lo-yen of Hiuwen Thsang…if, as f have supposed, the Asylum Stipa was really situated on ‘the large flat island in the middle of the mouth of the Ghaghra River…the site of the Kumbh4n stipa should really be looked for among the mounds of ancient ruins at Cheran
note: Differs from Cunningham 1871 and Mizutani (Narayana temple at/above Revelganj; asylum stupa at Chapra; Drona stupa Deghwara, which Carlleyle rejects). Argument runs to p. 79

author: Carlleyle
asr_identification: Dharmaranya (and Dharmaoli) at Baliya, Ganges N bank
evidence: Kan-phata (slit-ear) etymology; Bikapura village washed away; old Ganges channels (river shifting south)
quote: The Dharméranya (and Dharmaol), at Baliya, identified as the site of the Aviddhakarna Monastery of Hiuwen Thsang, and the Vast Solitude (or Wilderness) of Fa-hian
note: Same locality as Cunningham 1871 and Mizutani (near Ballia), but on different evidence: Dharmaranya tank and Dhamaoli rather than Bikapur

author: Carlleyle
asr_identification: Dharmaranya Pokhra tank, c. 450 ft N of the NE corner of Baliya town, with traces of old jangal
evidence: site surveyed by Charitra Lall under the Officiating Tahsildar; names Dharmaranya and Dhamaoli; Bikapura and Bhagrasan engulfed by the river
quote: 1 saw several mounds of ruins at, or in the immedia neighbourhood of, Baliya, and [ felt certain I had correctly identified the site I wasin search of, more especially from tw names still existing there, namely, Dharmaranya and Dham aoli
note: Agrees in locality with Mizutani and Cunningham (Baliya); revises the Bikapur name-link

author: Carlleyle
asr_identification: Dharm-aranya monastery at Baliya: mounds near Wazirapur, Dhamaoli and Muhammadpur
evidence: mounds measured: Wazirapur 165 ft circ., c. 14 ft high; Dhamaoli 283 ft circ., c. 13 ft; Muhammadpur 300 ft circ., 24 ft (possible stupa); Ganges then further south; Xuanzang's crossing near Nainijor/Dharmangathpur
quote: I think there cannot be any doubt tha I have identified the site of the monastery mentioned b Hiuwen Thsang and Fa-Hian, and that its real original nam must have beén Dharm-4ranya
note: Baliya locality agrees with Mizutani/Cunningham; Bikapur replaced by Dharmaranya

author: Smith (V. A.)
asr_identification: programme: fix Kapilavastu relative to Tauliva, Nigliva, Tilaura-Kot, Lori-ki-kudan; plot city and gates; locate Krakuchandra and Konagamana stupas
quote: The explorer should first try and fix the position of the city of Kapilavastu, asa whole, as accurately as possible, in relation to points within British territory, to Tauliva, Niglivd, and the great mounds at Tilaura-Kot, Lori-ki-kudan
note: Smith's prefatory note (instructions to Mukherji); no identification yet

author: Smith (V. A.)
asr_identification: Rummindei mound (Nepal Tarai), containing the eight stupas of Xuanzang
evidence: Mukherji's excavation of a buried temple (plinth, Pl. XXI-XXII); Nativity group of sculpture photographed and drawn; head of Maya recovered outside the shrine
quote: Mr. Mukberji’s researches at Rummindei, the site of the Lumbini Garden…would no doubt disclose the eight stupas enumerated by Hiuen Tsiang, which were evidently all comprised within the limits of the existing mound of ruins
note: Agrees with Mizutani; revises Cunningham 1871 (Mokson)

author: Smith (V. A.)
asr_identification: Rummindei = Lumbini; river of oil = Tilar Nadi; split Asoka pillar = the inscribed pillar beside the nativity temple
evidence: Rummin = Lummini of the inscription; Tilar Nadi (tel = oil); tank c. 25 paces S of the nativity shrine; pillar split down the middle (lightning), inscription states Buddha was born here; nativity sculpture
quote: (2) Hiuen Tsiang notes that the little river which flows past the garden to the south-east is locally called “the river of oil.”…That little river is to this day the Tilar Nadi…The site of the Lumbini garden is therefore fixed with absolute certainty
note: Agrees with Mizutani; revises Cunningham 1871 (Mokson; Kohana river)

author: Smith (V. A.)
asr_identification: Kapilavastu 9-16 miles W of Rummindei; Sravasti not Sahet-Mahet but where the Rapti leaves the hills NE of Nepalganj (Führer: Materiya, left bank)
evidence: pilgrims' bearings tabulated (Sravasti c. 90-100 miles NW of Kapilavastu)
quote: Kapilavastu, the city of the father of Gautama Buddha, was frem 9 to 16 miles distant from the Lumbini garden, in a westerly direction…I venture to think that I have succeeded in demonstrating that Suhet-Mahet on the borders of the Gond4 and Bahraich districts in Oudh cannot possibly be Sravasti
note: Śrāvastī rejection differs from Mizutani and Cunningham 1871 (Sahet-Mahet); argued in JRAS 1898, 1900; later abandoned

author: Smith (V. A.)
asr_identification: Kapilavastu of Xuanzang = city round Tilaura-Kot on the Banganga (citadel = Tilaura-Kot; area Lori-ki-kudan, Gutiva, Sagarwa, Nigliva, Araura-Kot); Kapilavastu of Fa-hian = Piprava; Krakuchandra's town = Palta Devi (alt. S of Chandapar); Konagamana's town = Sisania Panre (Nigali pillar moved from there); Nigrodha grove = Gutiva; massacre of the Sakyas = Sagarwa; Isvara temple = Tauleshvara at Tauliva; arrow-well not identified; Ramagrama 200 li E of Lumbini
evidence: compass arcs from Rummindei (9 miles cuts Piprava, 14 miles cuts Tilaura-Kot); Tilaura-Kot c. 1 mile circuit; Führer's 17 small stupas at Sagarwa with weapon-marked bricks; broken pillar worshipped as Mahadeo at Palta Devi (possibly Asokan); Nigali Sagar embankments repaired
quote: Pipraya is the Kapilavastu of Fa-hien…Primdé facie, then, the Tilaura-Kot group of ruins is the Kapilavastu of Hiuen Tsiang…The Konagamana pillar is doubtless that now lying at the Niga&li Sagar. It was probably removed from Sisania
note: Two-Kapilavastu theory. Tilaura-Kot agrees with Mizutani; Kanakamuni town at Sisania (pillar moved) differs from Mizutani (Nigali Sagar pillar). Revises Cunningham 1871 (Nagar). new: massacre of the Śākyas, Īśvara temple

author: Smith (V. A.)
asr_identification: Sravasti in remote forest near Nepalganj; Kusinagara in the interior of Nepal beyond the first range; Ramagrama capital N or NNE of Nichlaul near Dharmauli (Nepal); ashes stupa = great stupa at Lauriya Nandangarh (Champaran); Krakuchandra's town at Palta Devi or near Chandapar
quote: Kusinagara must, in my opinion, be far in Kusinagara. the interior of Nep4l, and certainly across the first range of hills…The capital will, I think, be found in Nepalese territory near the frontier, north, or a little east of north from Nichlaul police station
note: Kusinagara and Śrāvastī differ from Mizutani and Cunningham 1871 (Kasia; Sahet-Mahet); ashes stupa at Lauriya Nandangarh differs from Cunningham 1871 (Sahankat)

author: Smith (V. A.)
asr_identification: Rummindei mound with the eight stupas; Ramagrama NNE of Nichlaul near Dharmauli (alt. Bawan Garhi, Champaran); ashes stupa = Lauriya Nandangarh; Vaisali = Basarh
quote: I think it more probable that Ramagr4ma will be found about north-north-east from Nichlaul in Nepalese territory, near Dharmauli…Lauriy4-Nandangarh (Navandgarh), which I think represents the ‘ashes stupa,”
note: Vaiśālī = Basarh agrees with Mizutani and Cunningham

author: Smith (V. A.)
asr_identification: Piprava group = Kapilavastu of Fa-hian (Xuanzang's at Tilaura-Kot)
evidence: Peppé's Piprava relic stupa and inscription; Rhys Davids' independent argument
quote: My identification of the Piprava site with the Kapilavastu of Fa-hien rests upon the pilgrim’s description of his itinerary
note: Postscript (June 1901)

author: Mukherji
note: Lalita Vistara legends (arrow-well, Hastigarta); no location

author: Mukherji
note: Asoka's pilgrimage and the Isvara/Yaksha temple legend; no location

author: Mukherji
note: Sakya migrations and chronology

author: Mukherji
note: Chronological table

author: Mukherji
asr_identification: Tilaura-kot = Kapilavastu; NW mound = palace; 16-sided structure NE of it = Asita stupa
evidence: excavation at Tilaura-kot: octagonal and square structures, 16-sided solid brick structure with portico, cruciform structure; N gate c. 100 ft N
quote: Since, almost at first sight, I thought that Tilaura-kot might represent the ancient aud now forgotten Kapilavastu, and the north-west mound, the site of the palace
note: new: Asita stupa. Tilaurakot agrees with Mizutani; revises Cunningham 1871 (Nagar)

author: Mukherji
name_in_asr: Kapilavastu; place of massacre of the Sakyas
asr_identification: rejects Führer's extent of Kapilavastu (Jagadispur, Bikuli, Srinagar, Ahirauli, Ramapur, Singurh, Ramghat); Sagarwa stupas = Führer's massacre site
evidence: walked the area: ruins only at Sagarwa forest, Bikuli and W of Ahirauli; two Sagarwa stupas 'not fully excavated'
quote: The rows of Stupas were identified by Dr. Fuhrer as the “ Place of Massacre of the Sakyas”…In fact, Dr. Fiihrer’s identifications are full of contradictions
note: new: massacre of the Śākyas

author: Mukherji
asr_identification: rejects Führer's Bikuli temple (Abhayadevi) as the Isvara temple; Nigali pillar in the W embankment of Nigali Sagar, 1 mile S of Nigali village
evidence: Bikuli: carved bricks, lingas, temples (octagonal, saptaratha), no Parvati figure; Nigali pillar in two portions; embankments restored when the tank was re-excavated
quote: The fact is that the temple cannot be identified with that of Isvara ; as not only it stood out of the way, but Bikuli did not form the eastern orany boundary of Kapilavastu
note: new: Īśvara temple

author: Mukherji
asr_identification: Rummindei: temple of Mayadevi on the birth site
evidence: temple plinth exposed c. 8 ft below the plateau; sandstone Mayadevi group 5½ x 3½ ft (Mauryan style)
quote: The temple of Mayadevi, of which the exqtisite plinth I exposed some 8 feet below the level of the plateau, must, therefore, have been built . subsequent to the decay of the original fane, but long before the visit of the Chinese pilgrims
note: Agrees with Mizutani

author: Mukherji
asr_identification: Piprava = Sakya colony after Virudhaka's sack, not Kapilavastu; Piprava stupa = Sakya relic stupa
evidence: Piprava inscription; broken stone box and caskets (reopened, ascribed to Asoka)
quote: But the Chinese pilgrims did not see this Stupa at Kapila. vastu, which fact shows that it was not there
note: Against Smith's Piprava = Fa-hian's Kapilavastu

author: Mukherji
asr_identification: Kapilavastu c. 10 miles W of Rummindei, N of the Nigali and Gutiva pillars; Rummindei certain
evidence: Rummindei pillar in situ (strata)
quote: Fifty i, or about 10 miles west of Rummin-dei, Kapila. vastu should, therefore, be searched for. In this direction, the Nig&li and Gutiva pillars define the locality further

author: Mukherji
asr_identification: Kapilavastu = Tilaura-kot on the Banganga (citadel/royal precincts = brick fort; outer town Chitra-dei, Ramghat, Sandwa, Tilaura); palace = NW area of the fort; Kanakamuni town at Araura; arrow-well at Sisania or Piprava; Piprava, Sisania, Saina-Maina, Araura-kot rejected
evidence: fort walls 9-12 ft thick, circuit c. 5,200 ft; palace foundation c. 5 ft below ground; medieval remains round the Samai-mayi temple; octagonal and square buildings E of the temple
quote: These calculations lead me to look All evidence narrowing the field of discovery f0r Kapilavastu at the Kot of Tilaur4…It will thus be seen that no other ancient site has so much claim on the identification of Kapilavastu as Tilaura
note: Agrees with Mizutani (Tilaurakot). Emends 50 li to c. 20 li (S to Krakucchanda). new: palace of Śuddhodana, conception vihāra

author: Mukherji
name_in_asr: Stupa of Asita; vihara of Rahula's mother; school-house
asr_identification: Asita stupa = 16-sided structure NE of the octagonal one, Tilaura-kot; Yasodhara's quarters NW of the central tank; school NE of the central tank
evidence: 16-sided solid brick structure with portico; buildings excavated near the central tank
quote: I traced the foundations of two edifices—one sixteen-sided and the other cruciform in plan…I at once concluded that this must have been the Stupa of Asita
note: new: Asita stupa, Yaśodharā's chamber, school-house

author: Mukherji
asr_identification: Sangharama = building in front of the E gate of Tilaura-kot; Deva temples at Chitra-dei; elephant stupa = mound c. 500 ft S of the S gate; Hastigarta = ditch 100 ft E of it
evidence: foundations of a large building excavated in front of the E gate; large temple exposed at Chitra-dei
quote: I searched for the remains of a quadrangular structure, and I found one just in front of the eastern gate…About 500 feet south of the south gate of the citadel is a small mound of earth which might represent the elephant-throwing Stupa
note: new: saṅghārāma by the royal precincts, deva temples, elephant pit

author: Mukherji
asr_identification: Nigrodha monastery = Lori-Kudan, c. 2 miles S of Tilaura-kot; Kashaya and conversion stupas = the other Lori-Kudan mounds; Kanthaka's return stupa c. 650 ft SE of the E gate
evidence: solid brick stupa-like mound and 40-ft structure at Lori-Kudan; large stupa SE of the E gate
quote: But about 2 miles further south are the ruins of Lori-Kudan, where is a solid brick ‘mound, very like a Stupa…This structure might represent the famous Nigrodha monastery
note: Smith puts the Nigrodha grove at Gutiva. new: Kanthaka stupa, kāṣāya stupa, vihāras of the four signs

author: Mukherji
asr_identification: Isvara temple = Tauliva-isvara linga temple; tournament stupa at Derwa; massacre = Sagarwa (with Führer); ploughing stupa near Jadi on the Jamuar; Krakuchandra's town = Gutiva (Asoka pillar stump 'Phuteswar Mahadeva', brick stupa); Kanakamuni pillar = Nigali near Nigliva
evidence: Gutiva brick stupa with Asoka-pillar stump, bones dug by Waddell; large mound NE of Gutiva village; Sagarwa: 17 stupas and 49 compartments (Führer)
quote: If I am justified in reducing the distance from 50 to about 20 J’, or about 4 miles…then the ruins at Gutivi answer well our purpose of identification ; for here is a brick Stupa, near which is the lower portion of an Asokapillar
note: Krakucchanda at Gutiva differs from Smith (Palta Devi); Mizutani gives no site for 06.02.05. new: Īśvara temple, tournament stupa, massacre of the Śākyas

author: Mukherji
asr_identification: Kanakamuni's town = Araura-kot or the Thamua quarter by the Nigali Sagar (pillar in situ); arrow-well = Sisania (alt. Piprava); Lumbini = Rummindei
evidence: no brick stupa near the pillar; Thamua (< stambha) village on mounds; ancient tanks; small mound at Sisania; Nigali Sagar re-dug
quote: the bricks might have been removed from the Stupas for the rebuilding of the Arfur4-kot, which, I think, represents the town of the Muni…Sisanid may, therefore, be the more probable site for the Arrow-well
note: Kanakamuni near the Nigali Sagar pillar is close to Mizutani; differs from Smith (pillar moved from Sisania). Arrow-well: Cunningham 1871 Sarwanpur

author: Mukherji
asr_identification: Rummindei: Sakra stupa and four Devaraja stupas among the small stupas found; split pillar 45 ft W of the Mayadevi temple; river of oil = Tilar; Lumbini-grama = elevated plot S of the mounds; Koli/Devadaha = Koliha rivulet near Baghia
evidence: five small stupas excavated; pillar and bell capital split; Tilar stream 1½ furlongs E; vestiges of tanks to the W
quote: The pillar is about 45 feet west of the back-wall of Mayadevi’s temple and, as noted by Hiuen Tsiang, itis split in the middle…there is a small stream about a furlong and half east of the mound still called Tilar
note: Agrees with Mizutani; revises Cunningham 1871 (Kohana). new: stupas of Śakra and the four Devarājas, Nāga springs

author: Mukherji
asr_identification: Sravasti near Nepalganj (Smith) to be explored; Ramagrama probably N of Gorakhpur district; Kusinagara = Mukherji's 'Pari-nirvana spot at Lowriya' (alt. Smith's Deo Darpa)
quote: The end of the season might be devoted to the search for Kusinagara at Deo Darpa…if my identification of the Pari-nirvana spot at Lowriy& does not hold good
note: Kusinagara: Mukherji rejects Kasia (cites Smith); differs from Mizutani and Cunningham 1871
